summary: This defines a RobotPet class that stores a pet's name, battery level, and mood, and can perform a generic trick. It is the code under test for the unit tests in this section.

lines.text: This is the blueprint for every robot pet in the chapter; the tests you write will create instances of it and check their behaviour.
The constructor runs whenever you write something like RobotPet("Rex", 100, "happy"), and it receives the three starting values for the new pet.
Copying the argument onto self stores it on the object itself, so the name survives after the constructor finishes.
The battery level is kept as an attribute so later methods, and later tests, can read and change it.
The mood is the third piece of state a test can assert on after calling a method.
A method that returns a description of what the pet does; returning a string rather than printing it is what makes it easy to test.
The base pet has no special skill, so it returns a fixed sentence. The f prefix does nothing useful here because there are no braces to fill in, but it is harmless.
